Chapter 8: Motherhood and the Inheritance of Pain
Becoming a parent—it opens up a whole new kind of vulnerability, doesn’t it? There’s this fierce urge to protect your child from every cruelty the world might throw at them. But just as powerful is that fear: what if you end up passing along your own pain? Memories from childhood—maybe of loss, maybe of fear or feeling out of place—they never disappear completely. Instead, they linger at the edges of your choices, shaping what you hope to give your child: things you might’ve missed out on yourself, like safety, stability, and unconditional love.
The very first time your child looks up at you, trusting you completely, something deep inside you changes. The responsibility can feel overwhelming, almost heavy. But at the same time, there’s this huge sense of purpose. Every day becomes a balancing act. You’re always weighing how much you should shield your child, and how much you should prepare them for the world outside. How long do you hold them close before letting go? Suddenly, the world seems even more dangerous, and the stakes feel impossibly high.
And sometimes, old wounds resurface when you least expect it. Maybe you snap in frustration, and your words come out harsher than you meant. Or you catch yourself feeling a flash of anger that sounds a little too familiar. The guilt hits fast and hard. There’s always that worry—what if I’m repeating the same patterns I grew up with? But then, there are these gentle moments of grace. Reading a bedtime story together, sharing a laugh, or whispering a quiet reassurance in the darkness. It’s in these small, everyday moments that healing really happens—for both you and your child.
Most people don’t realize how much invisible work goes into breaking those old cycles. It’s not just about putting food on the table. It’s about learning new ways to love, and making a conscious choice not to let the past dictate the future. The process? It’s messy, it’s imperfect, and it never really ends. There are days when it feels impossible, when the weight of what came before is just too much. But there are also days when hope takes over—when you really believe that a different future is possible.
In the end, motherhood is an act of faith. It’s the promise to keep trying, over and over, to do better. To love, to forgive, and to keep moving forward. Yes, the inheritance of pain is real. But so is the inheritance of resilience. The story of motherhood isn’t just about what gets passed down—it’s about what’s transformed along the way.
